status: fixed before any Rust full-model training run
scope: R2P step 4: connect the full SmallForecaster (C128/H32/V3/D64/L2, full series attention) to the training graph on artificial data only. Not CARE/MetroPT/demand data, not formal R2, not R1.
dtype: CPU float32; every literal below is an integer divided by a power of two, so Python and Rust build bit-identical inputs
parameter_names: the 59 trainable tensors of crates/banto-ai/src/checkpoint.rs expected_shapes() except the buffers scale_floor, position and time_mask; 109024 values
name_salt: s(name) = (sum of the UTF-8 bytes of the tensor name) mod 257

initialization.rule: value of flat row-major element i of tensor name with salt s; no RNG
initialization.linear_weight: ((i*7919 + s) mod 257 - 128) / 128 * a, a = 1/8 when the input width (shape[1]) <= 64, else 1/16; applies to patch, head, blocks.*.temporal|variate.{q,k,v,out}.weight and blocks.*.ff.{0,2}.weight
initialization.linear_bias: ((i*31 + s) mod 17 - 8) / 256; applies to every *.bias of a linear layer
initialization.norm_weight: 1 + ((i*13 + s) mod 9 - 4) / 64; applies to blocks.*.norms.*.weight and final_norm.weight
initialization.norm_bias: ((i*11 + s) mod 7 - 3) / 64; applies to blocks.*.norms.*.bias and final_norm.bias

buffers.position: the float32 sin/cos table of small_model.py, saved in the reference as buffer/position and loaded by Rust; not trained
buffers.series_mask: all-true 3x3 (full series attention): variate attention applies no mask; in small_model.py it is a non-persistent buffer

batches.context: x[b,c,t] = ((t*(c+3) + 5*b + k) mod 16 - 8) / 4 + c for channels c=0,1; channel 2 is x = 2 + ((t + b + k) mod 2) / 16 so that its standard deviation (1/32) is below scale_floor[2] and the floor binds

procedure: build parameters and buffers from the rules above
forward batch A; loss = training_loss of small_model.py: pinball on normalized quantiles against (actual - context_center) / context_scale, mean over B*C*H*3
backward; gradients of all 59 tensors (none may be missing)
global norm clip, max_norm 1, coefficient min(1, 1/(norm+1e-6)); no optimizer update
independently, forward batch B with the initial parameters and report its loss

compare.raw and clipped gradients over all 59 te: gradient global relative L2 (or the zero-reference L2 rule)

reference.independent_check: the same model and procedure in float64 from the same float32 inputs; the float32 Torch values must meet the comparison tolerances against it, or generation stops

rules: the Rust forward used for training must be the same code path as inference (SmallForecaster), returning tensors to the loss without host readback
do not inject host-computed reference values into the Rust graph; buffers and initial parameters are inputs, not outputs
a failure is recorded and stops; do not change this fixture, the tolerances or the toy to fit Rust results
passing this step is not R1 or formal R2; R1's one unmet intermediate value stays unmet

not_compared.parameters and moments after an AdamW up: excluded before freezing. One AdamW update of the full model is ill-conditioned under the one-step tolerance: AdamW divides by sqrt(v)+eps, so where |gradient| is near or below eps the update depends on rounding. tools/r2p_full_model_adamw_probe.py reproduces it: 5 of 177 parameter/moment tensors differ between float32 and float64 beyond the tolerance, at most 1.1e-5 (atol 1e-6). The largest come from an element with |gradient| about eps (blocks.1.temporal.v.weight, 1.05e-8 vs 1.22e-8) and from head.bias elements whose float64 gradient is exactly 0 at a pinball tie (float32 2.3e-10); the attention key biases, whose gradient is structurally zero because softmax is invariant to a shift shared by all keys, differ by up to 2e-6. The return plan defines step 4 as loss and all-parameter gradients; AdamW itself is verified in steps 2-3.

clip_note: At this fixture the global gradient norm is about 0.958 < 1, so the clip coefficient is exactly 1 and the clipped gradients equal the raw ones. The full-model comparison therefore checks the norm and that clipping leaves gradients unchanged below max_norm; the scaling branch (norm > max_norm) is covered by R2P step 2 (cases C2/C3 and O3).
